newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: France urges Daewoo to bid again for Thomson unit.
newsitem.headline: France urges Daewoo to bid again for Thomson unit.

text.p: France hopes Daewoo Electronics will bid again for Thomson Multimedia and would be sympathetic to any offer, a visiting French presidential envoy said on Wednesday.
"The French government is hopeful that Daewoo will re-enter a bid," the envoy, Jean-Claude Paye, told a news conference.

"Since Daewoo already once made a near-successful bid, we are sure that it would be looked upon with sympathy, but of course without preference, because the process must be transparent and without prejudice."
Paye added that France would reopen the privatisation process after a European Community commission made a decision on a planned recapitalisation of the ailing state-owned Thomson SA.

"The commission wants to be sure that the recapitalisation doesn't distort competition at the expense of other companies," said Paye, who added he did not know when the commission would make a decision.
"The French government will then decide on whether or when to go ahead with privatisation."

Paye said while it was theoretically possible Thomson's privatisation could be cancelled "it is quite clear that the government does not want to retain the assets of this company in the public sector".
Paye said during a second privatisation effort, Daewoo would be able to make a case directly to the independent privatisation committee.

"During the second round, Daewoo will be able to directly deal with the committee because Thomson Multimedia will be sold off separately," he said. Defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF would be handled differently.
This would avoid any miscommunication or confusion about Daewoo's ability to take over the firm, which may have coloured the committee's decision during the first privatisation attempt, Paye said.

Paye also said France would return to South Korea historical documents now in French museums in exchange for other cultural artifacts, an issue that has added fuel to anti-French sentiment following the Thomson sale fiasco.
Details of the exchange had not been worked out, he said.
